newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Shell cautious after flat Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Shell cautious after flat Q1 profit.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported flat first quarter earnings on Thursday and said oil prices might fall further from recent highs with refining margins staying under pressure.
Shell said earnings excluding special items edged up by one percent in sterling terms to 1.545 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) from 1.535 billion a year ago.
A combination of lower gas sales, higher taxes and the pound's strength offset higher oil production profits and a strong chemical performance.
Overall earnings, which roughly met analysts' average expectations, would have risen by seven percent if measured in dollars, Shell said to illustrate the impact of adverse currency movements.

Shell's results came after U.S. oil companies last month surprised markets with strong results. But industry analysts said Shell's performance should not be taken as meaning the Anglo-Dutch group was lagging behind its U.S. rivals.
Any comparison should take into account that Shell's first quarter profits in 1996 were exceptionally high due to several one-off factors such as an unusually low tax rate.
Similarly, results were boosted a year ago by exceptionally cold winter weather in Europe. In contrast, mild temperatures early in 1997 led to a four percent drop in gas sales volumes, Shell said.
Despite this fall, profits in the exploration and production sector rose nine percent to 996 million pounds due to higher oil prices.
Refining and marketing profits fell one percent to 519 million pounds. Lower profits in the United States were largely offset by an improved performance elsewhere in the world, Shell said.

Chemicals earnings rose 12 percent to 184 million pounds due to further cost-cutting. The chemicals recovery may continue in the second quarter, the company said, but the longer-term outlook hinged on the ability to pass on higher feedstock prices.

Shell saw scope for oil prices to fall further as worldwide production increases were likely to exceed demand growth. An expected rise in global inventories might also weigh on oil prices after they had already started falling early this year, Shell said.
Analysts were not too upset by the company's downbeat comments, saying lower crude oil prices were already factored into the market.
If anything, Shell's oil price warning showed the group's prospects were better than many of its rivals, several analysts said.

Most competitors were far more geared towards oil production than Shell and were therefore more vulnerable to to lower crude prices, they said. "If you look at Shell's position they will do better than their peers if the oil price falls further," said one analyst.

Meanwhile, shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc were 7-1/2 pence down at 1,082-1/2 in late afternoon trading. Shares in Royal Dutch Petroleum fell 0.70 to 347.50 guilders in Amsterdam. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
